q7.answer: Workers do not get a push. They read billing_mode, which is a copy of the rollout record carrying its mode_epoch, and act on it only when that epoch matches the latest record they have read and only within T (15 minutes by default, D11) of that read; the controller re-copies a stale flag. The document does not say how often workers poll, and it does not say what happens to an invoice already in flight when a forward move changes the mode (only rollback drain and cutover handle in-flight charges explicitly).

q8.answer: The evidence lives in the rollout record: the shadow and both counters, each day's counted/not-counted result written within 24 hours, and the Finance sign-off with name and time. Moves are one step, made by a billing-owner member, logged in the audit log, and applied as a compare-and-set on the record version; the transition guards in the diagram (shadow gate passed, both gate passed plus sign-off) are what block an early move, though R1's explicit refusal list only names an open rollback and an unreadable record, so the gate-not-passed refusal should be stated in R1 when the controller is built.

q9.answer: The rate monitor detects the condition. It measures new-engine faults divided by charge attempts over a 10-minute window, with a 60-minute fallback when a window has fewer than N attempts (N = 50 by default, D4), and it fires when the rate is above 2 percent in both or new_only only. When it fires, it applies the fence at once (through the D12 path if config is down), pages on-call, and runs the precheck; if the precheck fails, the rollout enters d9_hold, and a person cannot abort an automatic rollback.

q10.answer: Charges that fall due are queued, never dropped (R7). From both or new_only neither engine charges while the rollback is open, so customers see a delay bounded by catch-up time before D; from shadow the old engine keeps charging throughout. After cutover to old_only, the old engine's normal charge run picks up the queued charges, skipping any customer-period that has a ledger charge, an in-flight charge, or a hold (R11).

q11.answer: Each charge carries an idempotency key derived from customer and billing period, the ledger allows at most one charge per customer per period, and the provider's idempotency key backs this (R6). The drain step resolves every unknown outcome against the provider by that key before any retry, and cutover skips any customer-period that already has a ledger charge or an in-flight charge. Mode and fence control which engine works but do not replace this guard.

q12.answer: Each rollback step is idempotent and resumable and records its progress (started_from, current step, actor, timestamps) in the rollout record. If a step fails, the rollback stays open with the fence up, on-call is paged, and the step is retried until on-call completes it or, for an on-call start, aborts at D; an automatic start enters d9_hold at D instead. If config is unreachable the rollout sits in record_pending with no cutover or reset until the record is written, and a failed cutover compare-and-set changes nothing, so it is re-read and retried.
